card.name: Inside drug names and appositive phrases
card.fires_on: Words inside a drug name, or the words 'a component of' / 'available' right after a drug name, in drug-label warnings. It fires where the text is about to repeat or continue a drug name.

modes.label: Appositive after a drug
modes.description: The words 'a' and 'component' in 'a component of' after a drug or class name.
modes.example: Gastrointestinal Bleeding, Ulceration, and Perforation NSAIDs,<< a>> component of naproxen and esome

modes.label: Partway through drug names
modes.description: A middle piece of a long drug name that is still being spelled out.
modes.example: angiotensin II receptor antagonists, including olmesartan medox<<om>>il, may result in deterioration of renal

modes.label: Words before a bracketed cross-reference
modes.description: A word in a clause that ends in a section reference, such as 'Dosage' or 'available'.
modes.example: SPRAVATO is<< available>> only through a restricted program under a REM

card.writes: No clear output effect; the promoted tokens are mostly code-like closers and fragments.
card.plain: It lights up inside long drug names and in short phrases like 'a component of' that point back to a named drug.
